nodes.summary: For a simple graph $G$ on a finite vertex set, a natural number $n$ and a set $s$ of vertices, this applies rounds of breadth-first search to $s$ (each round adds all neighbours of the current vertices), stopping after $n$ rounds or as soon as a round adds no new vertex, whichever comes first, and returns the resulting set.
nodes.title: Breadth-first search with a round limit

nodes.summary: For a simple graph $G$ on a finite vertex set and a set $s$ of vertices, this is the set of vertices that lie in $s$ or are adjacent to some vertex of $s$, that is, $s$ together with all neighbours of its vertices.
nodes.title: One round of breadth-first search

nodes.summary: In a connected graph every vertex `v ≠ s` has a neighbor `p` one step closer to `s` (a parent of `v` in a breadth-first tree rooted at `s`).
nodes.title: Parent vertex towards a root in a connected graph

nodes.summary: A simple graph $G$ is infinitely connected if it has at least two vertices and, for any two distinct vertices $u$ and $v$, there is an infinite set of paths from $u$ to $v$ in $G$ that are pairwise internally disjoint.
nodes.title: Infinitely connected graphs

nodes.summary: Two walks $p$ and $q$ in a simple graph $G$ are internally disjoint if no vertex is an interior vertex of both, where the interior vertices of a walk are the entries of its vertex sequence other than the first and the last.
nodes.title: Internally disjoint walks

nodes.summary: For a simple graph $G$ on a finite vertex set $V$ and a vertex $u$, this is the set obtained from $\{u\}$ by breadth-first search with at most $|V|$ rounds, stopping early as soon as a round adds no new vertex.
nodes.title: Vertices reachable from a vertex

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
